rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEM OF DISPOSITION OF SEIZED/ CONFISCATED ILLEGALLY CUT, GATHERED, REMOVED AND POSSESSED LOGS, LUMBER, FLITCHES, AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to curb this anomalous situation by PROHIBITING the DENR or the Natural Resources Development Corporation (NRDC) from conducting a public auction on al seized/confisca ted illegally cut, gathered removed and possessed logs, lumber, flitches and other forest products. Instead, these should be donated to the local government units having jurisdiction over the area of origin to benefit their respective communities. These forest products will be distributed according to priority, thus enhancing delivery of education, housing or infrastructure in the territorial jurisdiction of the LGUs concerned.
rows.status: Substituted by HB12658

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM INCOME TAXATION THE SALARIES OF MEMBERS OF THE JUDICIARY AND PUBLIC PROSECUTORS
rows.abstract: Rationale: This exemption is in support of a constitutional provision. Taxes diminish the salary of justices and judges.  Their salary is very inadequate given the inflationary cost of commodities and services, high tuition fee of students, and thelike. Their expertise and nature of work are comparable to veteran lawyers in the private practice whose minimum salary is Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00) every month. Lawyer researchers in private law firms get a starting salary of Thirty ThousandPesos (P30,000.00), while judges start at Nineteen Thousand Pesos (P19,000.00) every month.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PARAGRAPH TWO, SECTION 24 (A) (1) AND REPEALING SECTION 35 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997(RE: ZERO(0)-RATED INCOME TAXES)
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to provide for ZERO (0)-RATED INCOMES TAXES in lieu of the current system of personal exemptions. It will make our tax law more in consonance with the Constitutional mandate of progressivity. It will impose tax where tax is due.  Itwill provide for much needed relief to low-wage earners.  It offers a system administrativel y more feasible than the present one, with negligible reduction, if any, in revenues from income taxes.
rows.status: Substituted by HB12423

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A CHAMBER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY SYSTEM, PROMOTING ORDER, EFFICIENCY AND EFFECTIVE DELIVERY OF SERVICES BETWEEN AND AMONG CHAMBERS OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Chambers of Commerce and Industry Act of 1999".  The bill seeks to promote the growth of chambers of commerce and industry (CCIs) nationwide. Presently, there is no chmaber of commerce and industry system for all business and economic sectors. chambers have thus uncontrollably mushroomed across the country with overlapping and duplication of functions and services resulting in inefficiency, and inability to provide value added services for its members, among others. For purposes of enhancing the support of functions of CCIs in national economic growth, there is felt a need to establish a set of standards for greater efficiencies and effectiveness of Philippine CCIs.
